title: His first record and Henry Brown
summary: The first record 'Black but Sweet' with the Macs, made in New Orleans; talk of pianist Henry Brown.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Well, it was, it was, it was one of the, you know, one of the numbers. Do you remember about the first record that you ever made? I believe the first record I was made was Black But Sweet Old Gold. With the Macs. Macs. Was that made up in Chicago or down here? Right here. Right here.
Right here. Remember the studio, where it was cut?

I forgot where that was, but I don't believe it was on Cornell Street. I believe it was on either Barone or Carnell Street, something like that. It probably was Barone. Hmm? Probably was Barone, because I think Manuel Moneta made some records at the same time.
Yeah, that's what I think it was. Who would you piano play on there? There's a piano and trumpet. Piano and trumpet.
You're the trumpet, but I'm trying to remember what else is there.
Oh, there was some old piano by the name of Henry Brown. Oh, he was the one at the show. Yeah.
Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. He was another great blues man.

There's a Henry Brown that plays blues living in St. Louis now. Can you see him? I don't know. I don't know. I'll tell you how I find out about it. Roosevelt Sykes told me about it, you know. Might be him.
I don't know. Never got to know his father from Atlanta. Well, he died pretty soon. His name was Hemingway, James Hemingway. He played with us a couple of years, but he didn't live alone. He died.
Was he a trumpet player? No, piano. Piano player.
